definition: Self-management is the process by which computer systems manage their own operation without human intervention.
details: Self-management technologies are expected to pervade the next generation of network management systems. The growing complexity of modern networked computer systems is a limiting factor in their expansion. The increasing heterogeneity of corporate computer systems, the inclusion of mobile computing devices, and the combination of different networking technologies like WLAN, cellular phone networks, and mobile ad hoc networks make the conventional, manual management difficult, time-consuming, and error-prone. More recently, self-management has been suggested as a solution to increasing complexity in cloud computing. An industrial initiative towards realizing self-management is the Autonomic Computing Initiative (ACI) started by IBM in 2001. The ACI defines the following four functional areas: Self-configuration Auto-configuration of components Self-healing Automatic discovery, and correction of faults; automatically applying all necessary actions to bring system back to normal operation Self-optimization Automatic monitoring and control of resources to ensure the optimal functioning with respect to the defined requirements Self-protection Proactive identification and protection from arbitrary attacks

explainer.lead: Self-management is the process by which computer systems manage their own operation without human intervention. It matters as modern networked systems grow too complex and heterogeneous for manual management.

tiers.eli5: It is a system that runs its own housekeeping instead of waiting for a person to do it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply it to network management systems grappling with heterogeneity, mobile devices, and mixed networking technologies. The pitfall is that conventional manual management becomes difficult, time-consuming, and limiting as those systems expand.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it is the process by which computer systems manage their own operation without human intervention. Its motivation is that growing complexity is a limiting factor in the expansion of modern networked systems.

explainer.example: A network spanning WLAN, cellular, and mobile ad hoc links adjusts its own operation rather than leaving configuration to manual administration.
